solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Police officer oddly enraged grabbing monsieur?

indicators.note: grabbing says the rearranged word takes hold of another piece, which ends up inside it
oddly here means in a strange way, telling us the letters of enraged get rearranged

parts.note: M is the standard abbreviation for the French title monsieur

explanation.surface: A furious policeman seizes a Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like a pointer to odd letters, but here it is an anagram signal: ENRAGED becomes GENDARE, and 'grabbing' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gendarme is a member of the French armed police force.

clue.text: Like air eg Sousa played

indicators.note: music that is played is performed, and here the words eg and Sousa are performed in a new order

explanation.surface: Air on the radio, for example a march by Sousa being played.
explanation.walkthrough: John Philip Sousa was an American composer of marches; 'played' rearranges EG plus SOUSA.
explanation.definitionFit: Air is a gas, so something like it is gas-like in form.

clue.text: Rope put up in a moment — one's last?

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means raised from bottom to top, so the word is read upwards

parts.note: something happening in a moment happens soon

indicators.note: last here picks only the final letter of the word one

explanation.surface: A hanging rope rigged shortly before someone's final moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' turns SOON into NOOS, then E, the last letter of 'one', is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop of rope with a running knot, as used by a hangman.

clue.text: Unruly giants' action is actively hostile

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so the letters of the following words are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Badly behaved giants on the attack.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of GIANTS plus ACTION are rearranged; the apostrophe adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being antagonistic means opposing someone with open enmity.

clue.text: European nation involved in formal talks

indicators.note: involved in says the letters are contained within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A country taking part in official negotiations.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the join of 'forMAL TAlks'.
explanation.definitionFit: Malta is an island republic in the Mediterranean and a member of the EU.

clue.text: Primarily solid crust after bloodshed?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the first letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A hard layer that forms on a wound once blood has been shed.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters of 'solid crust after bloodshed' spell the answer, and the whole clue also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The dry protective covering that forms over a healing cut is exactly a hardened layer of dried blood.

clue.text: "Oh, heck, revolutionary verse writer from Russia

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning things over, so the letters of the exclamation are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry about a Russian poet of the revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' seems to point to Russian history, but it is the anagram signal for the exclamation; the verse abbreviation goes on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Anton Chekhov was a Russian playwright and short-story author.

clue.text: Elite accepting English harass constantly

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: the elite are the best of a group

explanation.surface: An upper class that lets the English in keeps pestering them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accepting' puts E inside BEST.
explanation.definitionFit: To be beset is to be troubled or attacked on all sides, persistently.

clue.text: Grasped a hope that's turned out to end badly

indicators.note: turned out suggests something rearranged or overturned, so the letters of the phrase are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone clung to a hope which proved to end in disappointment.
explanation.walkthrough: The twelve letters of 'Grasped a hope' are rearranged. The phrase is British slang: something goes pear-shaped when it fails.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal idiom means to go wrong or fail, as plans can.

clue.text: Cry out with United getting in attempt at goal

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a shot is an attempt to score in football
U is the usual abbreviation for United, as in football team names

explanation.surface: A football fan yells as United take a shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting in' puts U inside SHOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To bellow is to call loudly, the same as yelling.

clue.text: England footballer, one running with pride

definitions.meaning: the England women's football team are nicknamed the ...
a female big cat that hunts and lives in a group called a pride

explanation.surface: An England player who runs out with great self-respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pride' means self-respect in the surface but is the collective noun for a group of lions.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses name a female lion: literally in the wild, and as the nickname of the England women's team.

clue.text: Unit regularly installed in lounge

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture set in a sitting room.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of LOUNGE gives the answer; 'installed in' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A single whole thing counted as one item is a unit.

clue.text: What's used for firing at gophers on the rocks

indicators.note: on the rocks means wrecked or in ruins, so the letters of the fodder are broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: Someone shoots at burrowing rodents among the rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the rocks' reads as a location, but it rearranges AT GOPHERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Grapeshot was cannon ammunition of small balls packed together, fired from guns.

clue.text: Leave high and dry in London street

definitions.meaning: to abandon someone without help or means of getting away
a major thoroughfare in central London running from Trafalgar Square towards Fleet Street

explanation.surface: Being abandoned on a street in London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Strand is a well-known street in central London, home to the Savoy hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to maroon or abandon; the other is the name of a famous road in Westminster.

clue.text: Takes down concerning trousers

parts.note: re is a word meaning concerning or about

explanation.surface: Someone lowers a pair of trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes down' suggests removing trousers, but it means writes down.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something down is to note it in writing, which is to log it.

clue.text: Minor details of endless court case involving half a dozen in Rome

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one piece is placed inside another
endless says the final letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a court case is a trial
six is written VI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A lengthy Roman court case over half a dozen small points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts the last letter off the court case, and 'involving' wraps what is left round the Roman six.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivia are small, unimportant facts or matters.

clue.text: Judge rarebit to be cooked

indicators.note: to be cooked means to be prepared or altered, so the letters of rarebit are reworked

explanation.surface: A judge is told a Welsh cheese dish is to be cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh rarebit is a British dish of melted cheese on toast; its letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter decides disputes, as a referee or adjudicator does.

clue.text: Who'll replace key canal feature, this unfortunately divided by motorway

parts.note: a lock is a gated section of a canal used to raise or lower boats

indicators.note: divided by means split by something placed in the middle
unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so the letters of this are muddled

parts.note: M is the label of British motorways, such as the M1

explanation.surface: A canal lock fitting and a key, mangled where a motorway cuts through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunately' rearranges 'this' to SITH, and 'divided by' splits that with the motorway letter, giving SMITH after the canal feature.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who makes and fits keys and door fittings would replace a lost key.

clue.text: Fruit formed on elm

indicators.note: formed means shaped or made into something, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fruit growing on an elm tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ON ELM are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemon is a yellow citrus fruit.

clue.text: Country is US state that's abandoned North America

indicators.note: abandoned means left behind, so the named letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: Indiana is a state in the American Midwest

explanation.surface: A nation is described as an American state that left the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: INDIANA loses its final NA to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a large nation in South Asia.

clue.text: Fish of poor quality sent back

indicators.note: sent back means returned, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: something of poor quality is bad

explanation.surface: A diner returns fish that was not up to standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent back' turns BAD round.
explanation.definitionFit: A dab is a small flatfish.

clue.text: Note precipitation — and where it ends up?

parts.note: D is one of the musical notes
rain is water falling from clouds

explanation.surface: Rainfall and the place it finally flows away to.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers back to the rain: rainwater runs into a drain.
explanation.definitionFit: A gutter outlet or sewer is where falling water is carried away.

clue.text: Ready for honeymoon, arranged island in Med

indicators.note: in says the following pieces are placed inside the word for the sea

parts.note: Med is short for the Mediterranean, kept as written
arr. is the abbreviation for arranged, as in a music credit

explanation.surface: A couple about to honeymoon have booked an island in the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' looks like an anagram signal but is the music abbreviation; 'in' places it and the island letter inside the sea's short name.
explanation.definitionFit: A newly wed couple are the ones who go off on a honeymoon.

clue.text: Factory machinery set in position

definitions.meaning: an industrial works or manufacturing site
heavy equipment used in industry or building
to put something firmly in place in the ground

explanation.surface: Equipment installed at a works.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses of one word: an industrial site, its heavy equipment, and the verb meaning to fix firmly in place.

clue.text: Secluded retreat, simple and unpretentious but no house

indicators.note: but no means without, so the named letters are left out of the word

parts.note: honest can mean plain and without pretension, as in honest food

explanation.surface: A homely hideaway with no actual building.
explanation.walkthrough: HONEST loses HO to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A snug hideaway is figuratively a bird's home, cosy and private.

clue.text: Gather in about a third of debris for horticulturist

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to garner is to gather in, as a harvest

indicators.note: a third of picks the first two of the six letters of debris

explanation.surface: Collecting bits of rubbish for someone who tends plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A third of' a six-letter word means its first two letters; 'about' makes the gathering word go round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tends plants and grounds is an expert or worker in horticulture.
